newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -CHOPPY BUNDS EYE RESISTANCE AT 102.44.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -CHOPPY BUNDS EYE RESISTANCE AT 102.44.

text.p: September Bund futures traded on LIFFE will remain within their sideways range but will seek a test of the upside in the early part of Thursday's session, technical analysts said.

"Bunds are a bit choppy," said Christian Bado, senior technical analyst at Ferrier Lullin in Geneva. "We have been in a consolidation phase for more than a week now and will look for a test of 102.44."
On daily charts 102.44 was the high on August 4 and marks the top of the recent trading range.
At 0723 GMT September Bunds were at 102.15, up 0.24.
If Bunds break above 102.44, Bado said 102.80 would come into play.
"But failure to get through 102.44 would mean another downside move to 101.60 before seeing even further losses to 101.20," Bado said.
Technical analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London said Bunds had slipped on Wednesday to test trendline support around 101.72.
A failure to hold that level would take the contract down to a bear trigger at 101.50/43, they said.
"Losses through the latter would negate any lingering potential for an extension of the upside correction to 102.51," they said in a research note.
To the upside, the 102.51 level, a 50 percent retracement of the decline from the July highs, was likely to mark the limit of upside activity.
"Any additional corrective activity is expected to be short-lived (one-two days), before a resumption of recent declines," they said.
At the short end, December Euromarks were at 96.43, down one basis point on the day.
